absent: System-call entry, argument validation and error codes for creating events and establishing mappings.
Kernel-side scheduling, multiplexing, overflow handling, interrupt processing and counter-driver behavior.
Privilege, capability and access checks governing cross-task, system-wide or restricted monitoring.
Exact binary offsets, padding, alignment and bitfield order beyond logical field sequence.
Remainder of record-type details not in this part, including symbol-type codes, loader-event codes, stack limits and chain-context values.
Filter expression syntax and loader-program attachment and lifetime rules.
Throttle accounting and refresh interaction details.

findings.text: Monitoring request descriptor opens with a class selector named type, then a length field named size that enables forward and backward negotiation, then a primary selector named config with later extensions for hardware-specific growth. Growth slots are named config1 and also named config2 and also named config3 and also named config4. Payload selection uses a mask named sample_type for per-sample elements and a mask named read_format for counter readback composition. Branch refinement uses a selector named branch_sample_type, while separate fields choose user register coverage, interrupt register coverage, user stack extent, clock source, auxiliary watermark and auxiliary sample extent.

Sample detail fields bound captured machine state. One mask named sample_regs_user selects user registers. Another mask named sample_regs_intr selects registers at interrupt or sampled instruction. A length named sample_stack_user bounds user stack bytes. A clock selector named clockid chooses the time base when enabled. Auxiliary handling uses a watermark named aux_watermark and a per-sample extent named aux_sample_size. A limit named sample_max_stack caps call-chain or branch depth. An opaque value named sig_data is reflected to signal delivery for tool correlation.

Lifetime handling starts from a marker named disabled that requests creation in stopped state. Propagation uses a marker named inherit for descendants, narrowed by a marker named inherit_thread to thread-group clones, with a marker named inherit_stat requesting per-task aggregation. Residency uses a marker named pinned demanding constant hardware presence and a marker named exclusive demanding sole occupancy. Program replacement interacts through a marker named enable_on_exec that arms activation and a marker named remove_on_exec that detaches on replacement.

Counting scope can suppress categories. A marker named exclude_user omits unprivileged execution. A marker named exclude_kernel omits supervisor execution. A marker named exclude_hv omits hypervisor execution. A marker named exclude_host omits host side. A marker named exclude_guest omits guest side. A marker named exclude_idle omits idle time. Chain capture can omit supervisor portions via a marker named exclude_callchain_kernel and user portions via a marker named exclude_callchain_user. Address accuracy uses a two-bit selector named precise_ip for progressively stricter skid limits.

A toggle named mmap requests executable mapping reports. A toggle named mmap_data extends to data mappings. A toggle named mmap2 requests inode-enriched mapping reports. A toggle named build_id selects identifier form for those reports. A toggle named comm requests naming reports. A toggle named comm_exec flags replacement-driven naming. A toggle named task requests creation and termination reports. A toggle named context_switch requests switch reports. A toggle named namespaces requests namespace reports. A toggle named cgroup requests grouping reports. A toggle named ksymbol requests kernel-symbol reports. A toggle named bpf_event requests loader reports. A toggle named text_poke requests code-modification reports.

Sampling and delivery modes use further toggles. A toggle named freq selects frequency-driven rather than period-driven sampling. A toggle named watermark selects byte-threshold wakeups rather than count-driven wakeups. A toggle named write_backward requests reverse growth of the record area. A toggle named aux_output diverts production into auxiliary storage instead of ordinary records. A toggle named sigtrap requests synchronous trap delivery on events. A toggle named defer_callchain requests postponed chain capture. A toggle named defer_output enables emission of postponed chains. A toggle named use_clockid enables the chosen clock for time fields.

Overlaid storage reuses slots by role. One overlay holds either a count named sample_period or a rate named sample_freq. Another holds either a count threshold named wakeup_events or a byte threshold named wakeup_watermark. Breakpoint type in a field named bp_type pairs with an address slot holding either a hardware address named bp_addr, a probe symbol named kprobe_func, a user probe path named uprobe_path, or an extension named config1, plus a length slot holding either a length named bp_len, a probe address named kprobe_addr, a probe displacement named probe_offset, or an extension named config2. Auxiliary control overlays a raw word named aux_action with a bit named aux_start_paused for paused start, a bit named aux_pause for overflow-driven pause, and a bit named aux_resume for overflow-driven resume.

Loader-identifier query uses a header with an input length named ids_len bounding caller storage and an output count named prog_cnt reporting available programs, followed by a flexible array named ids that receives identifiers. The split separates caller-provided capacity from kernel-reported availability.

Control channel exposes operations on an event handle. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_ENABLE requests activation. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_DISABLE requests deactivation. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_REFRESH requests a refresh. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_RESET requests a reset. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_PERIOD updates sampling interval. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_OUTPUT redirects records. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_FILTER installs filtering expression. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_ID retrieves unique identifier. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_SET_BPF attaches loader program. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_PAUSE_OUTPUT suspends emission. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_QUERY_BPF lists attached loader identifiers. Operation PERF_EVENT_IOC_MODIFY_ATTRIBUTES adjusts creation parameters.

Encodings share a dollar-sign group with small indices from zero through eleven in creation order, distinguishing void controls from ones carrying payloads. Interval update, filter installation, loader attachment, output pause and attribute adjustment carry caller-to-kernel data, identifier retrieval carries kernel-to-caller data, and loader query is bidirectional. A group flag named PERF_IOC_FLAG_GROUP with least-significant-bit value extends single-event semantics to the whole group for activation, deactivation, budget extension, zeroing and interval update.

Shared control page starts with a version field named version and a compatibility floor named compat_version. A sequence field named lock coordinates tearing. A hardware selector named index distinguishes multiplexed from active states. A bias named offset is added to hardware readings. One accumulator named time_enabled tracks active duration. Another accumulator named time_running tracks scheduled duration. The pair supports scaling of time-shared counts. A size field named size reports header extent up to extension space.

Capability advertisement uses a wide word named capabilities with decoded bits. One bit named cap_user_rdpmc authorizes direct counter reads, gated by a width field named pmc_width for sign handling. A bit named cap_user_time enables cycle-to-time conversion through coefficients. A bit named cap_user_time_zero enables timestamp-to-cycle inversion through a base named time_zero. A bit named cap_user_time_short enables narrow-clock correction through a base named time_cycles plus a mask named time_mask. Conversion coefficients live in a shift named time_shift and a multiplier named time_mult and an offset named time_offset. Legacy reservation uses a bit named cap_bit0 defined zero and a bit named cap_bit0_is_deprecated defined one.

A field named data_offset locates ordinary record start. A field named data_size gives ordinary extent. A cursor named data_head tracks kernel production. A cursor named data_tail tracks user consumption. A field named aux_offset locates auxiliary start. A field named aux_size gives auxiliary extent. A cursor named aux_head tracks auxiliary production. A cursor named aux_tail tracks auxiliary consumption. Placement requires auxiliary start at or beyond the end of the ordinary area, and mapping extent matches auxiliary size. Reserved padding aligns the fixed header to one kilobyte.

Consistency relies on a sequence protocol plus ordered ring updates. Sequence coordination uses a field named lock. Readers sample that sequence, issue ordering barriers, copy timing and counter inputs, then retry on change, which confines accurate direct reads to self observation. Ordinary producer cursor is named data_head and ordinary consumer cursor is named data_tail. Readers apply a read barrier after observing the producer cursor, and writable mappings require a full barrier between payload inspection and publication of the consumer cursor, during which the kernel promises not to overwrite unreleased bytes. Auxiliary producer cursor is named aux_head. Auxiliary consumer cursor is named aux_tail with identical barrier and non-overwrite discipline.

Record annotation reserves low three bits as execution-context class. Defined classes are unknown, supervisor, user, hypervisor, guest supervisor and guest user, corresponding to successive small values from zero through five. Mask named PERF_RECORD_MISC_CPUMODE_MASK isolates the class. Individual names are PERF_RECORD_MISC_CPUMODE_UNKNOWN for unknown, PERF_RECORD_MISC_KERNEL for supervisor, PERF_RECORD_MISC_USER for user, PERF_RECORD_MISC_HYPERVISOR for hypervisor, PERF_RECORD_MISC_GUEST_KERNEL for guest supervisor, and PERF_RECORD_MISC_GUEST_USER for guest user.

A bit named PERF_RECORD_MISC_PROC_MAP_PARSE_TIMEOUT signals mapping-parse timeout. Bit thirteen appears as PERF_RECORD_MISC_MMAP_DATA for data mappings, as PERF_RECORD_MISC_COMM_EXEC for replacement-driven naming, as PERF_RECORD_MISC_FORK_EXEC for replacement-driven creation, and as PERF_RECORD_MISC_SWITCH_OUT for switch-out direction. Bit fourteen appears as PERF_RECORD_MISC_EXACT_IP for precise addressing, as PERF_RECORD_MISC_SWITCH_OUT_PREEMPT for preemptive switch-out, and as PERF_RECORD_MISC_MMAP_BUILD_ID for identifier-form mappings. Bit fifteen named PERF_RECORD_MISC_EXT_RESERVED reserves extension space.

Every record opens with a header named perf_event_header carrying a numeric kind, annotation bits and total length. Namespace linkage uses a pair named perf_ns_link_info with a member named dev for device and a member named ino for inode. Positions are named NET_NS_INDEX for network, UTS_NS_INDEX for UTS, IPC_NS_INDEX for IPC, PID_NS_INDEX for process identifier, USER_NS_INDEX for user, MNT_NS_INDEX for mount, CGROUP_NS_INDEX for control group, with NR_NAMESPACES giving the count.

When the attribute requests universal identity, each record appends a trailing identity block after its payload so older tools can ignore the suffix. The block conditionally carries process and thread identifiers, timestamp, unique and stream identifiers, processor number, and a position-stable duplicate of the unique identifier. The duplicate exists so parsers can locate identity at a fixed distance from the record length without decoding variable payloads.

Kind PERF_RECORD_MMAP reports executable mappings with start, length, file offset and pathname. Kind PERF_RECORD_MMAP2 enriches that with protection, flags and either filesystem identity or build identifier. Kind PERF_RECORD_COMM reports naming. Kind PERF_RECORD_FORK reports creation with parent and child identifiers plus timestamp. Kind PERF_RECORD_EXIT reports termination with parent and child identifiers plus timestamp. Kind PERF_RECORD_NAMESPACES reports a count followed by device-inode pairs. Kind PERF_RECORD_CGROUP reports identifier plus pathname. Kind PERF_RECORD_KSYMBOL reports address, length, kind, flags and name. Kind PERF_RECORD_BPF_EVENT reports loader kind, flags, identifier and tag. Kind PERF_RECORD_TEXT_POKE reports address, old and new lengths and concatenated bytes.

Kind PERF_RECORD_SAMPLE carries selected sample fields. Kind PERF_RECORD_LOST reports identifier plus dropped count. Kind PERF_RECORD_LOST_SAMPLES reports dropped sample count. Kind PERF_RECORD_READ carries process context plus readback values. Kind PERF_RECORD_THROTTLE marks throttling entry with time and identifiers. Kind PERF_RECORD_UNTHROTTLE marks throttling exit with time and identifiers. Kind PERF_RECORD_AUX reports auxiliary offset, extent and flags. Kind PERF_RECORD_AUX_OUTPUT_HW_ID disambiguates auxiliary producers via hardware identifier. Kind PERF_RECORD_ITRACE_START marks trace start with process context. Kind PERF_RECORD_SWITCH reports direction via annotation alone. Kind PERF_RECORD_SWITCH_CPU_WIDE adds next or previous process context. Kind PERF_RECORD_CALLCHAIN_DEFERRED carries a cookie plus address list for stitching with earlier supervisor-only chains.

Numeric record kinds run consecutively from one through twenty-two. Corresponding enumerators are PERF_RECORD_MMAP for one, PERF_RECORD_LOST for two, PERF_RECORD_COMM for three, PERF_RECORD_EXIT for four, PERF_RECORD_THROTTLE for five, PERF_RECORD_UNTHROTTLE for six, PERF_RECORD_FORK for seven, PERF_RECORD_READ for eight, PERF_RECORD_SAMPLE for nine, PERF_RECORD_MMAP2 for ten, PERF_RECORD_AUX for eleven, PERF_RECORD_ITRACE_START for twelve, PERF_RECORD_LOST_SAMPLES for thirteen, PERF_RECORD_SWITCH for fourteen, PERF_RECORD_SWITCH_CPU_WIDE for fifteen, PERF_RECORD_NAMESPACES for sixteen, PERF_RECORD_KSYMBOL for seventeen, PERF_RECORD_BPF_EVENT for eighteen, PERF_RECORD_CGROUP for nineteen, PERF_RECORD_TEXT_POKE for twenty, PERF_RECORD_AUX_OUTPUT_HW_ID for twenty-one, and PERF_RECORD_CALLCHAIN_DEFERRED for twenty-two.

Several sharp edges affect portability and sizing. Raw sample bytes are explicitly unstable across event, hardware and version and must not be treated as durable interface. Branch history may include per-entry counters whose presence and width depend on separate architectural parameters. Call-chain depth must stay below a system-wide ceiling and branch depth below hardware capacity. Signal correlation data truncates to native word size on narrow architectures. Narrow hardware clocks need mask-based reconstruction, while unaware readers still function only if no wrap occurs. Header-size and version fields must be honored for forward compatibility, and reserved words must be treated as zero.

Auxiliary capture follows a paused and running discipline. Creation can request starting paused, overflow can request automatic pause, and overflow can request automatic resume, allowing tools to bound capture around interesting intervals. Throttling uses paired entry and exit records bracketing intervals of suppressed sampling. Separate control operations request activation, deactivation, refresh and reset.

User entry consists of a control handle manipulated by indexed operations plus a shared page and record areas established by mapping. Tools configure monitoring through the attribute descriptor, adjust it through modification and interval operations, direct output and pause it, attach loader programs, then consume ordinary and auxiliary rings through head and tail cursors while honoring version, capability and barrier rules.

Forward compatibility rests on explicit lengths and reserved space. Attribute length lets kernels detect newer tools and vice versa. Control-page version pair plus header-size field lets tools detect newer kernels. Fixed padding aligns the control header to one kilobyte for stable mapping of record areas. Reserved bit ranges and words exist for future toggles and capabilities and must be preserved untouched.
